statutes.act: Read With Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: This is an appeal by special leave against the judgment of the High Court of Bombay dated 5 December, 1966 dismissing in limine the appeal preferred against the judgment and order dated 16 August, 1966 passed by the Sessions Judge, Sholapur.
The appellant was accused, No. 1. He was convicted under section 302 read with section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to imprisonment for life.
Broadly stated, the charge against the appellant was that he in conspiracy with his brother, accused No. 2 committed murder of Revansidhappa Shivappa Patil and Mahadeo Sidran Patil.
The defence of both the appellant and his brother was one of total denial.
issues: Whether the appeal raises arguable and substantial points
Whether the High Court should give reasons for rejection of appeal
petitioner_arguments: That a gross illegality was committed in relying upon the evidence given by a co-accused in a dacoity case
Denial of an opportunity to an appellant in a dacoity case of being heard as required under section 479A of the Criminal Procedure Code
respondent_arguments: That there were serious infirmities in the evidence and the manner in which the keys were recovered was open to objection
court_reasoning: The Appellate Court undoubtedly has power of summary dismissal
If the appeal raises arguable and substantial points, the High Court should give reasons for rejection of appeal
Rejection of an appeal by using only one word of dismissal causes difficulties and embarrassment in finding out the reasons which weighed with the High Court in dismissal of the appeal in limine
holding: The appeal is allowed. The order of dismissal of the appeal is set aside. The matter is sent back to the High Court for fresh consideration on hearing the parties.
